name: Chili heat
question: Scoville heat units: how many times an extract must be diluted before you can't taste the burn.

items.name: Banana pepper
items.fact: Banana peppers are so mild that some taste almost sweet.

items.name: Cubanelle
items.fact: Cubanelles are a favorite frying pepper in Cuban and Italian cooking.

items.name: Poblano
items.fact: Dried poblanos are sold as ancho chiles.

items.name: Jalapeño
items.fact: Smoked, dried jalapeños are called chipotles.

items.name: Serrano
items.fact: Serranos are a few times hotter than jalapeños.

items.name: Cayenne
items.fact: Cayenne is usually sold ground into powder.

items.name: Gingerol (fresh ginger)
items.fact: Ginger's bite comes from gingerol, which acts on the same heat receptor as chili.

items.name: Bird's eye chili
items.fact: Bird's eye chilies are a staple of Thai cooking.

items.name: Piperine (black pepper)
items.fact: Piperine is what makes black pepper make you sneeze.

items.name: Habanero
items.fact: Habaneros are hot but famous for their fruity flavor.

items.name: Red Savina habanero
items.fact: The Red Savina held the world record for hottest pepper through the 1990s.

items.name: Ghost pepper
items.fact: The ghost pepper was the first pepper measured at over one million SHU.

items.name: Police pepper spray
items.fact: Pepper spray strength depends on how much it's diluted.

items.name: Carolina Reaper
items.fact: The Carolina Reaper was bred in South Carolina by crossing two very hot peppers.

items.name: Pepper X
items.fact: Pepper X took the hottest-pepper world record from the Carolina Reaper in 2023.

items.name: Nonivamide
items.fact: Nonivamide is a synthetic capsaicin often used in pepper spray instead of chili extract.

items.name: Pure capsaicin
items.fact: Pure capsaicin is the benchmark at the top of the scale.
